item.title: DRU-Mixer: An Explainable Dilated Recurrent Unit-Based Mixer Model with Focal Loss for EEG-Based Interictal Epileptiform Discharges Detection
item.description: arXiv:2611.28030v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interictal epileptiform discharges (IED) have been identified as a core electroencephalogram (EEG) biomarker in diagnosing epilepsy patients. However, automatic detection and classification of IED require significant effort by human experts and can be prone to inter-rater variability. This paper presents Dilated Recurrent Units (DRU)-Mixer, a deep learning network to automate the process of identifying and classifying IED based on EEG recordings. The proposed architecture comprises a convolutional front end for extracting local features, dilated recurrent units modeling the temporal relationship between EEG signals, and mixer modules for token- and channel-level representation learning. DRU-Mixer was trained to perform (i) binary classification of IED/Non-IED segments and (ii) multiclass classification of regional IED types. For binary classification, DRU-Mixer showed 95.19% accuracy, 72.76% precision, 82.31% recall, 96.61% specificity, and 77.24% F1-score. For multiclass classification, the proposed network achieved strong sensitivity between 74.8% and 89.2%, as well as precision between 70.5% and 86.3%. Sensitivity-oriented analysis of the results shows that, for 70% sensitivity, DRU-Mixer provided 83.8% precision and 98.5% specificity outperforming VGGEEG and VGGSleep models and being on par with vEpiNet model. Interpretability of the model's results was estimated through occlusion mapping technique, which was used to highlight time intervals and EEG channels providing maximal contribution to the prediction. Maps generated by the technique show specific patterns for IED and Non-IED indicating that the model utilizes structured channel-time features corresponding to the presence of epileptiform activity.

item.title: Distributed Multimodal Monitoring and Prediction for PV Asset and Site Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2611.28034v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Utility-scale photovoltaic (PV) monitoring remains fragmented: electrical performance, structural condition and vegetation management are typically assessed through separate workflows, making it difficult to relate changes in energy performance to the local physical and environmental conditions experienced by individual modules. We propose a distributed multimodal monitoring and prediction framework that combines mechanical, optical, electrical, and microclimate measurements at the string level. Rather than treating these measurements as independent sensor streams, the framework uses them to derive higher-level indicators of asset and site condition, including quantities that are not directly instrumented. We designed and installed four compact wireless nodes attached directly to the rear of PV modules for a three-month pilot study to demonstrate module-level monitoring. From low-cost multimodal measurements, the system detected vegetation-management events, predicted wind speed from module vibration on unseen data, and extracted repeatable structural-frequency fingerprints associated with individual module locations. These preliminary results demonstrate a pathway from distributed monitoring toward predictive PV asset management, where multimodal observations can be used to predict or estimate otherwise unobserved operating and structural states, identify emerging changes earlier, and provide more granular intelligence than plant-level electrical monitoring or periodic inspection alone.
item.dc:creator: Jan Stiefel, Brendan Do, Reza Arablouei, Ross Dungavell, Brano Kusy, Kenrick Anderson, Benjamin Duck, Noel W Duffy, Peyman Moghadam

item.title: Multi-Epoch Batch Least-Squares Positioning on the Lunar Surface Using LuGRE GPS L1 C/A Pseudorange Measurements
item.description: arXiv:2611.28385v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Lunar GNSS Receiver Experiment (LuGRE) mission captured Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) signals in the lunar region, yielding position, velocity, and timing estimates. Analysis of onboard lunar-surface position estimates shows kilometer-level positioning errors due to the long propagation distances, limited measurements, and unfavorable GNSS geometry. This paper presents time-multiplexed positioning using publicly available LuGRE L1 C/A pseudorange measurements. The proposed approach accumulates measurements by exploiting the receiver's stationary position in the Lunar-Centered Lunar-Fixed frame after landing. The effects of the number of accumulated epochs, receiver altitude constraint using coarse a-priori information, straight-line tangential altitude threshold, and minimum number of measurements required per epoch are examined. Compared with single-epoch least-squares positioning, this approach substantially improves positioning performance using single-band, single-constellation signals. With selected combinations of these parameters, batches of epochs randomly selected from multiple operations yield 100-m-level accuracy at the 67th percentile.
item.dc:creator: Seunghwan Kim, Alex Minetto, Jacob Spagnolli, Fabio Dovis, Dennis Akos

item.title: Spectral-Leakage-Guided Phase-Noise Compensation for Sub-THz OFDM
item.description: arXiv:2611.28462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Oscillator phase noise is a key impairment in sub-THz OFDM, where it spreads energy across subcarriers and generates inter-carrier interference (ICI). Since the resulting leakage depends on both the oscillator phase noise spectrum and OFDM numerology, the useful compensation dimension varies with the operating configuration. This letter develops a leakage-guided receiver framework that relates these characteristics to the retained dimension of dominant-component Least Squares (LS) compensation and its clustered-pilot support. At 130 GHz with 64-QAM, the minimum tested order achieving BER <= 10^-6 decreases from 9 at 240 kHz to 3 at 960-1920 kHz for Hexa-X Model 2, while the first 3GPP crossing at 1920 kHz occurs with Np = 13 at 38 dB. Order adaptation reduces Stage-2 arithmetic by 66%, while four-cluster pilots improve 32-dB goodput by 35% over comb allocation.
item.dc:creator: Ahmadreza Afi, Didem Aydogan, Korkut Kaan Tokgoz

item.title: Asynchronous Uplink Rate Splitting Multiple Access
item.description: arXiv:2611.28466v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a two-user uplink system in which each user splits its message into layers and transmits them with deliberately chosen timing offsets, a scheme we call asynchronous rate splitting (A-RS). We show that timing offsets make the layers distinguishable only in the excess band of the pulse, where two spectral aliases overlap. For a root-raised-cosine pulse, the rate for every subset of layers has a scalar closed form that depends on the offsets through a single timing dispersion term. For fixed layer spectra and timing offsets, the achievable two-user rate region is a pentagon. Its two maximum-sum-rate corners are attained by successive interference cancellation that combines all matched-filter outputs at each decoding stage. Two layers per user, separated by half a symbol, are optimal for any delay between the users, and the spectrum of the user decoded last is a water-filling nested inside the water-filling of the total power. At high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), the optimal spectrum has twice the density in the excess band. By using the excess bandwidth of the pulse, which synchronous transmission leaves unused, A-RS achieves rate pairs outside the regions of both synchronous and asynchronous non-orthogonal multiple access. We implement a practical system with low-density parity-check codes which gives the weaker user $0.97$ bits per symbol more than any single-stream scheme at the same SNR.
item.dc:creator: Hossein Maleki, Hamid Jafarkhani

item.title: Energy- and Thermal-Aware Resource Management on Mobile IoT Endpoints: A Survey
item.description: arXiv:2611.28526v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Energy-aware and thermal-aware management of computing resources on portable and mobile Internet-of-Things (IoT) endpoints is still practiced pillar by pillar: radios, processors, and flash are optimized in isolation, yet sealed system-on-chip (SoC) products share sleep states, interconnects, and thermal limits. Pillar-local joule or temperature gains therefore often disappear after integration, and published savings are frequently incomparable. This survey asks how radio, compute, and storage should be coordinated so that deep sleep remains reachable, and which reporting rules make endpoint energy and thermal claims comparable. We synthesize literature from roughly 2000 to early 2026 with three instruments: a five-phase wireless power anatomy for power-aware networking; a four-branch taxonomy for collective power--performance optimization under mixed regimes; and eight evaluation gates that separate energy outcome, control cost, thermal feasibility, and evidence quality. We qualify the radio-limited premise with compute-, storage-, and thermal-dominated counterexamples, compare modeling and monitoring families, treat thermal behaviour as a shared constraint by separating sensing interfaces, compact models, throttling actuators, and the short-peak versus sustained-throttling regimes that reverse room-temperature rankings, give an illustrative phase-budget example with a sensitivity check and a model-selection workflow, and close with open problems on composability and reproducible measurement. The intended readers work on sustainable computing, mobile systems, and embedded energy management.
item.dc:creator: Yuchao Chang, Haoran Wei

item.title: VEGA: A Scalable Software-Hardware Co-design for Genome Alignment using RVV Extension
item.description: arXiv:2611.28741v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dynamic programming (DP)-based genome sequence analysis is fundamental to computational genomics, but it remains computationally intensive as genomic data volumes continue to outpace Moore's Law. Existing hardware accelerators often sacrifice programmability and scalability across diverse alignment algorithms. In this work, we present VEGA, a scalable software-hardware co-design that accelerates genome alignment using RISC-V Vector extensions. VEGA introduces specialized vector instructions and three key innovations: a Forefront Stationary dataflow that minimizes off-chip memory access, intersequence parallelism that maximizes SIMD lane utilization, and custom ISA extensions that accelerate core alignment operations. Evaluations show that VEGA achieves up to 15.1x and 9.7x speedups for Edit Distance and Smith-Waterman algorithms over the Ara2-RVV vector baseline, sustaining 10.2x and 6.7x gains for 10kbp sequences. Post-synthesis results indicate only 1.0% area overhead compared to a standard RISC-V core, with performance-per-area efficiency rivaling specialized ASICs. VEGA thus achieves a balanced advancement in efficiency, programmability, and scalability for genome sequence alignment.
item.dc:creator: Weihong Xu, Shijie Xu, Qunyou Liu, Giovanni Ansaloni, Cheng Zhuo, David Atienza

item.title: A General Non-Stationary Channel Model for Autonomous Vehicle Communications in Underground Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.28816v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous vehicles exhibit high mobility and environmental adaptability, making them well-suited for underground inspection and rescue missions. In this paper, a general three-dimensional (3D) non-stationary geometry-based stochastic model (GBSM) is proposed for autonomous vehicle communications in underground spaces. The proposed channel model accounts for the 3D mobility of autonomous vehicles and can be adapted to pillar, tunnel, and cave scenarios. To characterize the structural and physical features of underground spaces, the proposed model incorporates the generation and evolution of spatially dispersed and/or directionally confined clusters along with their constituent specular/dense multipath components (SMCs/DMCs). Additionally, the proposed channel model considers channel non-stationarity, waveguide effect, and near-field/far-field effects. Statistical properties, including space-time-frequency correlation functions (STF-CFs), delay/angular/Doppler power spectral densities (PSDs), root mean square (RMS) delay spread, and stationary interval, are derived and analyzed. The validity of the proposed channel model is substantiated through comparative analysis between measurement and simulation results.
item.dc:creator: Lin Hou, Cheng-Xiang Wang, Songjiang Yang, Hengtai Chang, Jie Huang, El-Hadi M. Aggoune

item.title: Merits of Collocating Uptilted Antennas on Terrestrial Base Stations for Aerial Coverage
item.description: arXiv:2611.28887v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The integration of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) into future wireless networks introduces challenges in ensuring reliable aerial coverage, particularly for UAV-based user equipment (UAV-UE). Traditional terrestrial base stations (BSs) with downtilted antennas, referred to as dt-BSs, are designed primarily for ground users. They provide inefficient connectivity to UAV-UE due to weak sidelobe gains, and susceptibility to ground reflection (GR) interference as well as sidelobe interference from non-serving dt-BSs. To address this, we propose a hybrid cellular architecture that collocates uptilted antennas on a portion of existing dt-BS towers, referred to as ut-BSs. These support UAV-UE exclusively, minimizing impact on ground users. We consider realistic antenna radiation patterns and probabilistic line-of-sight (LoS)/non-LoS (NLoS) links between ut-BSs and UAV-UE. Using stochastic geometry, we analyze the UAV-UE coverage probability, accounting for interference from both dt-BSs and non-serving ut-BSs, along with GR-induced interference. Results show significant improvements in UAV-UE coverage with only a small density of ut-BSs. GR interference is notable at lower altitudes but diminishes beyond 500 meters. This study highlights the potential of our hybrid architecture to enhance the reliability and scalability of UAV communications in large-scale deployments. It also offers actionable insights for telecom operators considering the collocation of uptilted antennas within existing infrastructure to better support aerial connectivity.

item.title: Multi-Sensor Fusion for False-Alarm Reduction by Timed Electromechanical Corroboration
item.description: arXiv:2611.29025v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A physician checks the clinical electrocardiogram against other observations. A wearable monitor has no physician. This paper shows that a mechanical sensor worn beside the electrocardiogram can take over that check, and that the right added sensors lower false alarms further. A beat is accepted only when a mechanical contraction follows at the delay learned for the wearer. Beat-shaped artifacts injected into resting and exercise recordings passed the electrocardiogram alone almost every time. A seismocardiogram or phonocardiogram as the second channel rejected most while keeping nearly all true beats, strongly at rest and partly during exercise. Shifting the mechanical signal in time removed the benefit. A detection criterion scores an added sensor by the part of its response that the sensors in place cannot predict. With four sensors, this score ranked the sets as their measured false-alarm rates did. With the two sensors it selected, 6.2 percent of the artifacts passed while 95 percent of true beats were kept, half the rate of the best single sensor. In integer arithmetic on a low-cost microcontroller, the detector made the same decisions as the software. These rates come from injected artifacts, not alarms in patients. Natural motion and clinical events remain untested.
item.dc:creator: Zixuan Fu, Anthony Raffaele, Unnikrishna Pillai

item.title: TrustFlow-ECG: Reliability-Aware ECG Restoration with Calibrated Risk Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2611.29084v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) restoration models can reduce noise and motion artifacts, but they rarely estimate whether the restored waveform is reliable for downstream analysis. We propose TrustFlow-ECG, a reliability-aware restoration framework that combines a one-step conditional rectified-flow restorer with a lightweight window-level risk predictor. The predictor uses the noisy ECG, restored ECG, and correction residual, then applies validation-set isotonic calibration for selective ECG analysis. We evaluate on MIT-BIH ECG windows corrupted with NSTDB artifacts, powerline interference, and mixed noise across multiple SNRs, with an external 9,675-window PTB-XL stress check without retraining. TrustFlow achieves 0.862 Spearman correlation with true risk and 0.911 AUROC for failure detection, while calibration reduces ECE from 0.0385 to 0.0098. At 80% coverage, selective rejection reduces RMSE from 0.1848 to 0.1345, improves R-peak F1 from 0.8778 to 0.9175, and reduces HR MAE from 6.26 to 4.88 bpm.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Kamel, Tamer Nadeem

item.title: Near-Field Physical-Layer Authentication Under Noisy Enrollment
item.description: arXiv:2611.29292v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In near-field physical-layer authentication (PLA), the receiver estimates a spatial reference from noisy enrollment pilots. With a fixed residual-energy threshold, even a small reference error can cause the false rejection (FR) probability to approach one as the received energy increases. We derive the distribution of the overlap between the true and enrolled spatial directions and use it to calibrate a test based on the aligned energy and the residual-to-aligned energy ratio. The calibration bounds FR for arbitrary regional gains and all legitimate received energies above a prescribed minimum. For a fixed enrolled reference, we reduce the problem of finding the maximum acceptance probability of a multi-antenna attacker to a one-dimensional search. We also derive a pre-enrollment upper bound that holds when the attacker chooses its precoder after observing the enrolled reference. For a single region and a fixed angular threshold, the enrollment energy sufficient to preserve angular separation grows inversely with the square of the available angular margin. In the numerical study with 128 receive elements at 28 GHz, the FR upper bound was 0.9984, including the enrollment outage allowance. At a regional phase perturbation of 20, four regions provided the best trade-off among the tested partitions: its simulated FR was 0.1442, while its false acceptance (FA) at 9 m was 1.084 under the fixed transmit-energy setting.
item.dc:creator: Parsa Rajabi, Mohammad Reza Abedi, Paeiz Azmi, Nader Mokari

item.title: WAFT: A Fourier-Analytic Framework for Steady-State Performance of Walker Constellations
item.description: arXiv:2611.29296v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Walker configuration is predominantly adopted by nongeostationary orbit constellations exemplified by Starlink and Kuiper. The steady-state distribution of aggregate downlink interference power is critical for spectrum coexistence regulation. Large-scale time-stepped simulation and stochastic geometry (SG)-based models are the mainstream methods for obtaining the distribution, but are either computationally expensive or subject to inherent bias. This paper models the aggregate downlink interference power as an additive observable and proposes the Walker-constellation Analysis via Fourier Transform (WAFT) framework to derive the steady-state performance. Modeling the constellation as a periodic impulse array on the phase torus, the spectral representation of the observable is derived via 2-D Fourier analysis. Analytical expressions for the expectation, variance, and steady-state complementary cumulative distribution function are further derived, and the periodicity of receiver performance along longitude is characterized. For a Starlink sub-constellation example, numerical validation shows that the percentile discrepancies of WAFT relative to a finite-duration time-stepped simulation remain within 0.09~dB. Comparisons with isotropic and intensity-matched SG models reveal that the conditional independence of satellite positions alone makes the models assign a substantial probability mass to physically infeasible values, producing percentile discrepancies.
item.dc:creator: Haoyang Xue, Bingkun Liu, Linling Kuang

item.title: On linear MMSE receivers in the presence of data-like multiuser interference
item.description: arXiv:2611.29370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Linear minimum mean-square error (LMMSE) receivers have been of great interest for many decades for multi-user interference (MUI) mitigation in radiocommunications networks in particular. Despite the extensive literature on this subject, this topic remains relevant to several current and emerging applications. In this context, the paper presents a continuous-time approach showing that most of LMME receivers of the literature are suboptimal. In particular, they are typically implemented at the symbol rate following matched filtering to the pulse-shaping filter and require a prior knowledge of the MUI channels, which can be difficult and costly to acquire in practice. The main contribution of this paper is to address the key challenge of designing new LMMSE receivers that achieve the performance of the optimal receiver without requiring prior knowledge of the MUI channels. To this end, two novel receiver LMMSE structures are proposed and analyzed for linearly modulated signals impaired by data-like MUI: a two-input receiver and a three-input receiver. The proposed receivers are shown to be quasi-optimal over a broad range of scenarios. These results provide new perspectives for practical implementation of the optimal LMMSE receiver in the presence of data-like MUI, relying only on knowledge of the signal-of-interest (SOI) channel.
item.dc:creator: Pascal Chevalier, Jean-Pierre Delmas, Roger Lamberti

item.title: A Closed-Form Soft Spectral Partition for Adaptive Mode Decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2611.29452v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Density-based Adaptive Mode Decomposition (DAMD) shows that the Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) objective, restricted to hard binary partitions, is equivalent to weighted K-means clustering, enabling automatic mode detection. The equivalence concerns detection only; extraction with hard Voronoi masks introduces boundary artefacts. This paper develops a soft extraction theory independent of the detector. First, the hard-partition equivalence is shown to be an algebraic identity that holds if and only if the weights are binary; hard and soft extraction are optima of two different functionals (linear K-means and regularised quadratic VMD) over the same simplex. Second, the regularised soft VMD problem is proved to have a closed-form global optimum, unique on the support of the spectrum: the Lorentzian-weighted partition $s_k^*(\omega)\propto[1+2\alpha(\omega-\omega_k)^2]^{-1}$. Every fixed point of the VMD ADMM mode update is proportional to $|\omega-\omega_k|^{-2}$; when the dual ascent enforces reconstruction, it is the $\alpha\to\infty$ endpoint of this family. The Lorentzian shape at finite $\alpha$ is therefore a consequence of the regulariser, and $\alpha$ controls how closely the allocation approaches that fixed point. Third, under a Lorentzian spectral prior the partition equals the minimum mean-square error (MMSE) estimator of each mode in the low-noise limit, tying $\alpha$ to the inverse squared mode bandwidth. Since the partition needs only detected centre frequencies, the extraction rule can be switched without recomputing detection. Synthetic experiments with known ground truth test the predictions; four categories of real signals show how much the two allocations differ.
item.dc:creator: Hao Jia, Chunyu Yang, Fan Feng, Cesar F. Caiafa, Feng Duan, Jordi Sol\'e-Casals

item.title: RF-Florence: Unified RF Detection and Physical Grounding with a Foundation Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.29496v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reliable signal detection is essential for spectrum sharing and intelligent sensing in sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks. Wideband radio-frequency (RF) monitoring must locate emissions and identify those satisfying waveform-family and physical constraints. The latter task, physical grounding, requires query meaning to agree with measurable signal attributes. RF-Florence unifies three tasks---full-scene detection, physical grounding, and supplied-region recognition---through a shared pretrained foundation model. Calibrated spectrograms connect localization coordinates to time and frequency, while common event targets and explicit predicates align task outputs with requests. On synthetic mixtures with family--attribute combinations withheld from training, structured queries improve mean grounding F1 by 7.66 percentage points over natural language. Under the tested two-path channel, direct grounding with structured queries exceeds a You Only Look Once (YOLO) detector followed by rule-based filtering by 3.44 points in mean F1. These results show the value of aligning query expressions with the signal families and physical variables that define the requested event set.
item.dc:creator: Mu Jia, Junting Chen, Pooi-Yuen Kam

item.title: Approximate Convex Decomposition (ACD) with Divide and Conquer Strategy for DRL-Based BS Localization
item.description: arXiv:2611.29503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optimal base station (BS) placement is a fundamental challenge in wireless localization. Conventional optimization approaches may become computationally demanding as the geometric complexity of the environment increases, limiting their scalability to realistic building layouts. This paper proposes an Approximate Convex Decomposition (ACD)-based divide-and-conquer framework integrated with deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for optimizing BS placement. The proposed approach exploits the geometric structure of building layouts by partitioning the original environment into smaller sub-regions using cuts associated with reflex vertices. Furthermore, the proposed solution is bench-marked against DRL without ACD and with the optimal solution obtained by exhaustive search. Results show the superiority of the proposed approach and that it approaches the optimal solution.
item.dc:creator: Omar Awad, Aly Morsy, Mohamed Shalma

item.title: DIBEM: Diffusion-Based Error Mitigation for Uncertainty-Aware UWB Localization
item.description: arXiv:2611.29656v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ultra-wideband (UWB) localization degrades substantially under Non-Line-of-Sight (NLoS) propagation, where multipath and obstruction induce complex ranging error distributions that are poorly represented by fixed parametric models. We propose Diffusion-based Error Mitigation (DIBEM), an uncertainty-aware framework that learns the conditional ranging error distribution directly from six compact Channel Impulse Response (CIR) statistics. Rather than predicting a deterministic correction or restricting uncertainty to a Gaussian or fixed mixture family, DIBEM uses a conditional diffusion model with denoising diffusion implicit model sampling to generate link-specific error samples. The resulting empirical distributions are incorporated into maximum likelihood position estimation. This allows localization to account for heterogeneous ranging uncertainty across anchor-tag links. Experiments across four indoor environments show that DIBEM achieves the lowest negative log-likelihood for NLoS ranging errors and the lowest or tied-lowest mean localization error across all environments. Compared with least squares approaches, DIBEM reduces mean localization error by up to 64.8 percent, while improving over Gaussian and mixture density probabilistic models by up to 15.8 percent and 14.0 percent, respectively. Results demonstrate the potential of diffusion-based conditional error modeling for uncertainty-aware UWB localization, particularly under challenging NLoS propagation.
item.dc:creator: Ghazaleh Kianfar, Maryam Hosseini, Arash Mohammadi

item.title: MedTimeQ: Query-guided fusion of time-series foundation models and LLMs for multi-lead ECG classification
item.description: arXiv:2611.29690v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate classification of medical time series, such as electrocardiograms (ECGs), requires capturing waveform morphology, long-range temporal structure, inter-lead dependencies, and clinical semantics. Existing large language model (LLM)-based approaches often map signal patches directly into the language embedding space, potentially underusing pretrained time-series knowledge and transferring redundant or irrelevant information. We propose MedTimeQ, a parameter-efficient framework that integrates a lead-aware temporal foundation encoder with an LLM-reprogrammed ECG pathway through gated residual fusion. A Query Former uses learned diagnostic queries to select and compress fused representations into informative soft tokens for a frozen LLM. Semantic prototype learning further guides classification through multiple clinical descriptions per category, statistics-based prompt selection, and knowledge distillation. Both foundation backbones remain frozen, limiting training to lightweight interface and classification components. We evaluate MedTimeQ on PTB-XL, Chapman-Shaoxing, and MIT-BIH for recording-level diagnosis, rhythm classification, and heartbeat classification, respectively. MedTimeQ achieves the best performance in 11 of 12 dataset-metric comparisons, with consistent class-balanced gains across all three tasks. On PTB-XL, it achieves 76.93% accuracy and 58.14% macro-F1, exceeding MedTsLLM by 10.08 and 7.07 percentage points, respectively. These results demonstrate the benefits of selectively integrating pretrained temporal representations with clinical language semantics. Code: https://github.com/kkianamm/MedTimeQ
item.dc:creator: Kiana Taktehrani, Maryam Hosseini, Arash Mohammadi

item.title: Blind Channel and Noise-Variance Estimation for MIMO Thermal Noise Modulation Systems via Generalized Expectation-Maximization
item.description: arXiv:2611.29758v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thermal Noise Modulation (TNM) is a communication paradigm in which information is conveyed through different thermal-noise variance levels rather than deterministic signal waveforms. Its stochastic nature makes conventional pilot-based channel estimation challenging, while pilot transmission introduces additional overhead and reduces spectral efficiency. This paper proposes a pilot-free blind receiver for M-ary TNM systems based on the Generalized Expectation-Maximization (GEM) framework. The proposed receiver jointly estimates the channel matrix, latent transmitted symbols, mixture probabilities, and unknown transmit-noise variance levels directly from received observations, without requiring pilot symbols or prior knowledge of the variance constellation. The modulation order M and receiver-noise variance are assumed to be known. Since the maximization step has no closed-form solution, a gradient-ascent procedure is incorporated into the GEM framework to iteratively update the unknown parameters. The proposed approach enables simultaneous channel estimation, symbol detection, and variance learning within a unified blind-receiver framework. Simulation results demonstrate accurate channel Gram matrix estimation and effective symbol detection without pilot overhead. Moreover, the proposed variance learning scheme achieves performance close to that obtained with perfectly known transmit variance levels, with only moderate BER degradation, demonstrating its potential for practical MIMO TNM systems.
item.dc:creator: Razieh Torkamani, Hadi Zayyani, Mohammad Salman, Felipe A. P. de Figueiredo

item.title: Extreme Value Theory for Peak Power in Discrete-Time Complex Gaussian Processes
item.description: arXiv:2611.29820v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The peak power for a band-limited, radio frequency (RF) signal, often expressed using the dimensionless peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR), is an important quantity for signal analysis and the design of RF transmitters and receivers. Modern digital instrumentation, like vector signal analyzers, collect and process discrete-time samples of the complex baseband signal. Also, computer-based simulations of continuous-time processes must be carried out with discrete-time sequences. Therefore, to design such measurements and simulations, accurate models for the distribution of the PAPR for discrete-time complex baseband processes are required. In particular, band-pass thermal noise and modern communication signals, like orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), are often modeled as complex Gaussian processes. To address this problem, we present a new analytical model for the PAPR distribution of a stationary, discrete-time, complex Gaussian process. We demonstrate that the new discrete-time model subsumes prior models based on asymptotic extreme value theory as special cases while providing a larger domain of efficacy. Specifically, using Monte Carlo simulations of filtered complex white Gaussian noise, we show that the new model is more effective for practical sample sizes and dual-band spectra than previous approaches.
item.dc:creator: Adam Wunderlich

item.title: Is Classical Error Control Ready for IMT-2030? Information-Loss Interfaces in Channel Estimation, FEC, CRC, and ARQ for Machine-Type Services
item.description: arXiv:2611.29842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fault tolerance and structured error control in mobile communication networks--historically implemented as a modular cascade of pilot-aided channel estimation (CE), forward error correction (FEC), cyclic redundancy check (CRC), and hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ)--remain foundational to 5G New Radio (NR). Although finite-blocklength coding, joint estimation-decoding, and grant-free access have been active academic topics for over a decade, commercial 3GPP specifications up to Release 18 still enforce rigid cross-layer boundaries between these blocks. In short-packet machine-type communications (MTC) for IMT-2030 (6G), inserting separate redundancy for channel training, error correction, and error detection shrinks the net payload entropy resolved per channel slot, while standardized UE processing timelines and HARQ round-trip delays collide with sub-millisecond reliability targets. Combining a multi-user MIMO short-packet simulation with real 3GPP TS 38.214 numerology latency budgets, this article diagnoses the structural bottlenecks of the legacy reliability pipeline and outlines an interoperable roadmap for 3GPP Release 20+--spanning soft-output universal decoding, sensing-assisted priors, grant-free joint detection, and task-oriented error control.
item.dc:creator: Igor B. Palhano

item.title: FL-CsLoc-DH: A Federated Learning-Based Crowdsensing Localization under Dual Heterogeneity
item.description: arXiv:2611.29867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mobile Crowdsensing (MCS) provides a scalable way to collect indoor fingerprints and reduce professional calibration effort. To protect the location privacy of participating clients, Federated Learning (FL) is used so that raw fingerprints and measurement trajectories remain local. However, owing to the open and uncontrollable nature of MCS, participating clients collect fingerprints in different propagation environments and possess unequal labeling availability. These conditions jointly cause data and annotation heterogeneity, which degrades FL-based crowdsensing localization. In this work, we propose FL-CsLoc-DH, a federated semi-supervised learning framework for crowdsensing localization under dual heterogeneity. FL-CsLoc-DH coordinates Two-Stage Noisy Gradient Rejection (TS-NGR), Soft Fisher Confidence Alignment (S-FCA), and Trajectory-Smoothed Model Averaging (T-SMA) throughout localization model learning. TS-NGR suppresses unreliable client updates caused jointly by environment dependent data shifts and noisy pseudo labels. S-FCA limits parameter increments dominated by unlabeled data, thereby alleviating annotation heterogeneity during local training. T-SMA smooths the aggregated global localization model trajectory to reduce drift induced by data heterogeneity. Experiment results show that the three mechanisms provide complementary improvements in localization accuracy under the MCS environment while retaining raw client data locally.
item.dc:creator: Xin Cheng, Binxu Wang, Zixuan Ai, Yuqing Yang, Yu He, Feng Shu, Guangjie Han

item.title: SA-GLRT-D: Sidelobe-Aware GLRT-Based Detector for FMCW Radar
item.description: arXiv:2611.30008v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates adaptive detection for frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar in multi-target complex scenarios, where reference-cell contamination, spectral leakage from the cell under test (CUT), and the resulting sidelobe interference severely degrade detection performance. A sidelobe-aware detector based on the generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT), termed SA-GLRT-D, is proposed. Unlike conventional filtering-then-constant false alarm rate (CFAR) schemes, the proposed method explicitly accounts for the non-ideal frequency-domain energy spreading of the CUT induced by the finite-window effect. Accordingly, conventional single-cell target detection is extended to local-region detection, and decision statistic construction, CUT-related parameter estimation, and sidelobe interference suppression are jointly accomplished within a unified hypothesis-testing framework. Furthermore, to reduce computational complexity, a fast implementation of SA-GLRT-D is developed, together with a dedicated parameter initialization strategy to enhance the stability of numerical optimization. Simulation and real-measurement results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high-accuracy target detection while maintaining a constant false alarm rate, with favorable computational efficiency.
item.dc:creator: Jiachen Zhu, Fangjiong Chen, Jie Wu, Ming Xia

item.title: One UWB Radar, Many Views: Comparing and Fusing Signal Representations for Human Activity Recognition
item.description: arXiv:2611.30033v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: IEEE 802.15.4z-compliant impulse-radio ultra-wideband (IR-UWB) transceivers are increasingly built into consumer devices, enabling contactless, privacy-preserving human activity recognition (HAR) in healthcare. Before activity classification, the signal is typically converted into range-time, range-Doppler, or time-Doppler maps, each exposing different spatial and motion cues. Existing comparisons often apply shared processing across representations, leaving it unclear whether their rankings hold after independent tuning. It is also unknown whether rankings and fusion gains generalize across environments and activities, and at what computational cost. Consequently, practitioners lack guidance on which representation and processing suit a given HAR deployment. We release an open dataset of raw IR-UWB measurements collected by a ceiling-mounted radar from 44 participants during scripted activity sequences in 12 layouts across two bedrooms. Using a statistically guided, staged search, we independently tune each representation across five processing and deployment settings. We then compare individual and fused performance under layout and room shifts and quantify computational cost. Across over 1{,}000 cross-validated models, independent tuning proves essential, as optimal processing differs per representation and processing choices shift macro-F1 by up to 26 points, four times the gap between representations. Once tuned, the range-Doppler map leads for unseen layouts (85.1\% macro-F1), while time-Doppler map does for unseen rooms (72.7\%). Fusing all three maps raises these scores to 89.1\% and 80.0\%, respectively. Lower sampling rates and narrower Doppler bands reduce latency by 38--51\% with at most a 1.5-point macro-F1 loss. The best representation for UWB HAR is therefore a deployment decision, not a fixed property.
item.dc:creator: Jelle De Moerloose, Anton Lambrecht, Adnan Shahid, Eli De Poorter

item.title: MIMO Integrated Sensing and Communications: A Fisher-based Local Mutual Information Approach
item.description: arXiv:2611.30051v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) beamforming requires a sensing utility that is compatible with the communication rate and aligned with per-target angle estimation. Fisher information (FI)/Cram\'er--Rao bound (CRB) criteria depend on the angular units and generally involve coupled multi-target matrices, whereas sensing mutual information (SMI) is typically defined on aggregate response variables. This paper proposes Fisher-based local mutual information (F-LMI), a prior-aware bit-domain utility for multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) ISAC. F-LMI linearizes each target-specific range-compressed statistic around the angular prior mean and yields a closed-form local information gain. In the single-target case, it admits a Bayesian CRB (BCRB) log-ratio interpretation and is a locally consistent surrogate for the nonlinear parameter MI. For multiple targets, the prior-induced variations of the non-intended targets are marginalized into a beamformer-dependent interference-plus-noise covariance in each branch. We derive a fractional-programming algorithm with linear-system updates and scalar bisection. Monte Carlo simulations with nonlinear target-wise posterior-mean receivers show that F-LMI reduces the root-mean-square error (RMSE) by 5.0--14.7\% relative to a target-indexed Bayesian-bound baseline at two matched rates in a closely spaced layout. Under a common basis-selection protocol, it also attains lower branch RMSE than aggregate and joint criteria.
item.dc:creator: Hyeonuk Kim, Jeongwoo Park, Nuria Gonz\'alez-Prelcic, ChanByoung Chae, Jeonghun Park

item.title: UV3CP: Universal ViT-Based 3D Channel Predictor for MIMO-OFDM Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.30128v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Channel aging in time-division duplex multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) systems causes a mismatch between uplink-based channel state information and the downlink channel at the transmission instant. Although vision transformers (ViTs) are effective for channel prediction, their performance is highly sensitive to the patch size, whose optimum depends on the channel coherence region. Moreover, changing the patch size typically requires retraining because it alters the token grid and patch embedding operator. In this paper, we propose a universal ViT-based 3D channel prediction framework, called UV3CP, for MIMO-OFDM systems. The proposed UV3CP employs an efficient 3D ViT backbone to capture frequency, time, and spatial channel dependencies. First, based on second-order channel statistics, we derive a statistics-aware patch-size selection rule that selects axis-wise patch lengths using a mean-squared-error-based criterion, thereby matching the tokenization granularity to the dominant channel coherence while controlling token length and complexity. Second, we develop a statistics-aware patch-embedding resizing method that enables a single shared UV3CP to operate across different patch sizes without patch-size-specific retraining. Simulation results show that the proposed method improves robustness under various scenarios and patch-size mismatch while reducing the need to train and store multiple patch-size-specific ViT models.
item.dc:creator: Sungyoung Ha, Yujin Kang, Seonjung Kim, Yo-Seb Jeon

item.title: Reciprocal Range-Doppler Estimation with Partial Path Association for Asynchronous Bistatic OFDM-ISAC
item.description: arXiv:2611.30221v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In bistatic integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), clock asynchronism shifts the delay and Doppler measured from orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) echoes. The two stations may see different reflectors, so the receiver must identify which echoes belong to the same path before combining the two views. For partial path association, PreVote finds a common displacement in the directional delay and Doppler differences. One-to-one assignment at this displacement accepts compatible pairs and allows other paths to remain unmatched. Each station uses coherent compression to form a subcarrier vector and a slow-time vector per path. For range-Doppler estimation in reciprocal sensing, the center multiplies paired vectors without conjugation. The opposite constant clock terms cancel, and a correct pair yields twice the physical phase slopes of one path. A Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) for fixed identities and phase branches quantifies the shared clock uncertainty. At the higher signal-to-noise ratios tested, reciprocal fusion yields lower range and Doppler errors than both receivers using calibrated echoes. Under partial visibility, displacement-based matching recovers more targets with correct identities and prescribed accuracy than separate centering with the same fusion stage. Balancing directional energy and extending the common aperture improve Doppler accuracy, while carrier frequency variation increases error.

item.title: Deep-Learning-Based Classiffcation of Relay-Surface Scattering Regimes for NLOS Millimeter-Wave Sensing
item.description: arXiv:2611.30279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In non-line-of-sight (NLOS) millimeter-wave sensing, relay-surface scattering alters target echoes and can cause propagation-model mismatch, angle-estimation errors, and ghost targets. DEKL, a deep-learning framework, identifies the dominant scattering regime from radar echoes without measuring surface roughness. Multipath echo models describe specular reflection, structured multipath reflection, and diffuse scattering. These models and a no-target hypothesis define a model-selection problem with unknown parameters. The Kullback-Leibler information criterion yields an adaptive decision rule for selecting among these hypotheses. A lightweight network, KLNet, learns covariance-domain features and combines attention with confidence-gated iterative decoding to avoid repeated likelihood evaluation. Analytical simulations, independent electromagnetic simulations, and radar measurements show that DEKL improves discrimination over the evaluated information-criterion-based rules. Ablations show how attention, confidence supervision, and gated decoding contribute to selective prediction and robustness under controlled covariance perturbations. The predicted regime guides propagation-model selection for radio-environment repre-sentations in wireless-network digital twins and informs NLOS localization and imaging.
item.dc:creator: Haoran Yuan, Guanghua Liu, You Xu, Zhihao Liu

item.title: Dynamic Channel Gain Map Reconstruction via Object-Attached Gaussian Propagation
item.description: arXiv:2611.30300v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Channel gain maps describe location-dependent propagation, but moving vehicles can change reception beyond their physical footprints. Reconstructing these changes requires connecting local object states to regional power. We consider a fixed transmitter and predefined receiver areas, with historical static and dynamic radio supervision and continuing delayed, noisy vehicle-state messages. We propose OA-GS, an object-attached Gaussian propagation model with a shared area correction. Each vehicle carries anisotropic kernels whose effective attributes are supplied by offline-calibrated templates and affine condition generators. Closed-form Gaussian integrals along finite propagation segments evaluate an effective attenuation model, while directional scattering terms account for additional power. These interactions modulate a learned static reference and contribute to regional channel gain. A shared multilayer perceptron then uses object, propagation, and receiver-area features to predict a bounded path-loss residual that compensates for errors in the compact propagation model. All learned parameters remain fixed during deployment, and reconstruction uses arrived vehicle messages without current-traffic radio measurements. In a fixed-scene ray-tracing study over four development traffic sequences and three initializations, OA-GS reduces map and strong-event dynamic-response root-mean-square errors (RMSEs) from 2.503 to 1.272 dB and from 5.965 to 3.563 dB, respectively, relative to a task-adapted GS-CG baseline receiving eight initial radio reports. The shared correction reduces strong-event dynamic-response error from 3.962 to 3.563 dB under the same propagation backbone, demonstrating the benefit of combining explicit propagation structure with learned regional correction.
item.dc:creator: Yi Wang, Junting Chen

item.title: Safety-Tiered ISAC Scheduling with History-Aware Value of Information for V2X Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.30420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) assisted vehicle-to-everything (V2X) networks prioritize safety-critical radar sensing over communication. However, existing scheduling methods overlook the varying criticality of vehicles, long-term fairness in service quality, and information staleness. Considering this, we propose a low-complexity sensing-prioritized allocation for radar and communication (SPARC-V) to maximize the value of information (VoI) in V2X networks. SPARC-V addresses these challenges with a two-stage hierarchical resource scheduling framework. For sensing, vehicles are first categorized into safety tiers based on a risk metric. Safety-critical vehicles receive orthogonal resources, while others can reuse resources under specific constraints. Sensing resources are allocated based on a sensing priority metric that balances safety significance and long-term fairness. In the next stage, communication resources are allocated to vehicles with the most outdated information. Performance is measured using a unified VoI metric that considers sensing quality, safety relevance, and information freshness. Monte Carlo simulations show that SPARC-V achieves the highest network VoI of 26.5 among all baselines, with its advantage over baselines widening as vehicle density increases.
item.dc:creator: Mubashar Sarfraz, Nima Imani, Spyros Lavdas, Constantinos B. Papadias

item.title: Combining Physical Layer Security and Symmetric Encryption to Secure Rate-Splitting Multiple Access
item.description: arXiv:2611.30428v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The demand for increased spectral efficiency (SE) in downlink multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) systems has led to the development of various multiple access techniques. Among these, rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) can improve SE over space division multiple access (SDMA) and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) by splitting each user's data into common and private parts. The common parts from all users are then encoded into a single common message, which is transmitted alongside the private messages using an RSMA-specific precoder. Recent results showed that the precoder can be modified to enable physical layer security (PLS) by integrating secrecy rate constraints into the design. However, this approach only secures the private messages, while the common part of each user remains unprotected. To address this limitation, we propose a hybrid-PLS RSMA scheme that symmetrically encrypts all user data and embeds key information within the PLS-secured private messages. Additionally, the RSMA precoder is adapted to ensure that the private messages are sufficiently sized to carry the key information. The precoder design is formulated as a non-convex SE maximization problem and solved using successive convex approximation (SCA). Analytical and numerical evaluations demonstrate that the proposed hybrid-PLS RSMA can significantly improve SE compared to partially secure RSMA and secure SDMA, when complete user data security is required.

item.title: Angular characteristics of attenuation and temporal dispersion introduced by single deciduous bush in winter conditions at FR2 band
item.description: arXiv:2611.30431v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vegetation-induced attenuation and temporal dispersion remain important impairments in millimeter-wave radio propagation, particularly in the frequency range 2 (FR2) band, where highly directional links are employed. Existing vegetation attenuation models, including ITU-R P.833, predominantly address scenarios involving trees or vegetation clusters and are typically derived for the main radiation direction of the transmitting antenna. This paper presents an experimental study of angular-dependent attenuation and temporal dispersion introduced by a single deciduous bush under winter conditions. Measurements were conducted on a university campus at 28 GHz and 38 GHz using a wideband channel-sounding testbed operating from 1 MHz to 44 GHz. The bush, approximately 3 m in height, was located at the center of a circular measurement trajectory with a radius of 10 m, along which the receiver was positioned at angular intervals of approximately 8 deg. Directional antennas with 7-9 deg half-power beamwidth were employed, and reception angles from 0 to 200 deg relative to the transmitter-bush axis were investigated. The results demonstrate significant angular variability in both excess attenuation and temporal dispersion, indicating substantial contributions from scattering outside the main propagation direction. Differences between the two carrier frequencies are analyzed, highlighting frequency-dependent attenuation mechanisms even in leaf-off conditions. The presented findings extend existing single-vegetation models by incorporating angular characteristics and temporal effects, providing valuable insights for the design and modeling of FR2 wireless links in sparse-vegetation environments.

item.title: Implicit Neural Representation for 3D Radio Map Compression in Low-Altitude Environments
item.description: arXiv:2611.30445v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low-altitude wireless networks require accurate 3D radio maps (RMs) to support environment-aware communication. However, due to the extensive spatial coverage and multi-modal channel representations, 3D RMs usually incur prohibitive storage and transmission overhead, making efficient compression highly desirable. In this paper, we propose NeRM3D, an implicit neural representation (INR)-based framework for compact 3D RM compression. Specifically, NeRM3D represents the entire 3D RM as a lightweight neural network that maps discrete height values to corresponding RM slices, thereby encoding the RM into a compact neural network. To effectively model the volumetric spatial structure of 3D RMs, NeRM3D jointly integrates horizontal embeddings with height-aware modulation, enabling efficient extraction and fusion of spatial correlations across different vertical layers and channel modalities. Experimental results demonstrate that NeRM3D achieves competitive compression performance with low complexity and decoding latency, making it suitable for resource-constrained devices.
item.dc:creator: Jiaming Cheng, Wei Chen, Yuchen Li, Bo Ai, Jun Zhang

item.title: Asynchronous Uplink Multi-UE Networked Sensing via Multipath Correlation
item.description: arXiv:2611.30528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiuser uplink sensing offers a promising paradigm for networked sensing by leveraging signals from multiple user equipment (UEs) to enhance sensing coverage and performance. This paper investigates asynchronous multiuser uplink orthogonal frequency-division multiple access sensing by exploiting correlated multipath structures across UEs. A common frontend first mitigates the dominant timing offsets (TOs), carrier-frequency offsets (CFOs), and phase offsets (POs) through LoS-referencing and constructs a reduced delay-angle-of-arrival (AoA) search space. Two alternative multiuser sensing estimators are then proposed, with different mechanisms of explicitly and implicitly exploiting UE correlation, respectively. The first explicitly adopts a latent-group shared-private sparse Bayesian learning (Group-SBL) model to exploit group-shared propagation structures while accommodating UE-specific components. The second combines calibrated multiuser observations for joint multiple signal classification (MUSIC) processing, recovering a global delay-AoA pool that can be further associated with individual UEs. Residual-TO refinement is conducted with both estimator updates, followed by local-grid delay-AoA refinement and residual common-phase compensation before Doppler estimation. Simulations under a 5G New Radio-compatible uplink configuration show that both multiuser schemes outperform their corresponding per-UE baselines, with larger gains as cross-UE propagation correlation increases.
item.dc:creator: Jingying Bao, J. Andrew Zhang, Kai Wu, Christos Masouros, Y. Jay Guo

item.title: Timestep Selection in Diffusion-Based OTFS Channel Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2611.30586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diffusion-based channel estimators are run with a few deterministic sampling steps, and their step count is treated as a knob that trades accuracy against latency. We show that for the mean squared error this trade-off mainly comes from the default leading timestep spacing, whose first timestep indicates an intermediate noise level although the initial state is pure noise. In a multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal time frequency space receiver with ray-traced paths and per-path Doppler shifts, moving only the first timestep of the default spacing to the pure-noise end recovers the gain of trailing spacing, completely for our anchored residual estimator and mostly for a published diffusion estimator. With trailing spacing one to three steps give the most accurate single trajectory of our estimator at every signal-to-noise ratio we test, and longer trajectories raise the error, by 0.34~dB over one step at a signal-to-noise ratio of 20~dB after 50 steps. This is the direction predicted by an idealized analysis in which a long deterministic trajectory turns the posterior mean into a posterior sample. With three trailing steps, the published estimator reaches 0.8 to 1.8~dB lower normalized mean squared error than with its original five leading steps, on its own trained network and test set. A start rule that places the first timestep from the error power of the linear anchor of the estimator, with one threshold per network, recovers trailing spacing for our estimator and matches start timesteps tuned separately for every signal-to-noise ratio on a noise-prediction network. A regression network with the same architecture and data reaches 0.23 to 1.36~dB lower normalized mean squared error than the best diffusion configuration we evaluate. The step count of a diffusion channel estimator should therefore be judged only after its first timestep is fixed.
item.dc:creator: Yi Luo, Dianxin Zheng, Ruixuan Mi, Xinqi Fu, Tianhao Guo

item.title: Optimal Window Design for Intercarrier and Intersymbol Interference Power Minimization in w-OFDM
item.description: arXiv:2611.30640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Block transceivers are essential for modern communication systems, and they are vastly implemented in many day-to-day devices, especially the orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) technique. The application of a pulseshaping technique in the OFDM generates the so-called windowed OFDM (w-OFDM). This letter proposes an optimization of the window shape, obtaining minimal intercarrier and intersymbol interference power, ICI, and ISI, respectively. A communication system is simulated by implementing the optimized w-OFDM, and its performance is compared with a non-optimized system using a raised-cosine window.

item.title: A Proposal for Multiplierless RLS Adaptive Filters with Implementation Complexity Constraint
item.description: arXiv:2611.30650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The so-called sum-of-powers-of-two arithmetic has the advantage of using simple shift and thus avoiding multiplications operations. In this work, we provide a feasible RLS adaptive filter algorithm employing the SOPOT representation. This reduces the computational burden of the RLS algorithm. Therefore, leading to a reduction in the power consumption from a hardware implementation point of view, which is an important feature in the developing of smaller, lighter and more power-efficient portable devices.

item.title: HEP-like 1550 nm wide-field pixelated optical receiver for inter-satellite laser links: a simulation-based proof of concept for Earth, lunar and Earth-Moon scenarios
item.description: arXiv:2611.28071v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: I propose and evaluate by simulation a wide-field dome optical receiver (a field of view larger than a hemisphere) at 1550 nm for the acquisition of inter-satellite laser links. The detector is an InGaAs pixel hybrid of about 1 Mpixel with event-driven, time-stamped readout, inspired by the pixel detectors of high-energy physics. A pulsed beacon is detected by the coincidence of m hits in a sliding block of pixels, and the angle of arrival (AoA) is estimated by clustering and centroiding and handed to a narrow-field data channel. In a 550 km Earth constellation, with a 5 mrad beacon and a 10 mm aperture, detection takes 12 $\mu$s to 2 ms (up to 116 ms with the 6-9 mm that the optics allow), with a whole-frame false-alarm rate below 0.01/s, and the AoA error is 0.13-0.23 mrad. Cooling to about 233 K gives a service life above 5 years for fluences up to about $2\times10^{9}$ p/cm$^2$ per year. The receiver is also studied around the Moon and on the Earth-Moon link, where it works only between high orbits. Compared phase by phase with published scan-based acquisition, the search phase (3-18 ms with 10 mm) is shorter by a factor of about $10^{2}$ to $10^{5}$; end to end, with assumed pointing and loop-closure times, it takes 0.16-1.5 s, comparable to a terminal with calibrated open-loop pointing but without requiring that pointing at the receiver; the partner's beacon must still be pointed at it to about 1.25 mrad (5 mrad beacon). All values are simulation results, obtained with idealised optics and a 1 Mpixel detector that does not exist today; none is a measurement.
item.dc:creator: Maurizio De Santis

item.title: A Multimode-Fiber Speckle Sensing Node with a Press-Robust Quantized Network for Liquid-Cooling Thermal Monitoring
item.description: arXiv:2611.28091v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Liquid-cooled AI and HPC racks concentrate heat at cold plates and manifolds, below the granularity of facility sensors. We present a self-contained edge node that turns one multimode fiber into a distributed thermal-event sensor over nine pipe segments, with a 450 nm laser, a camera and a Zynq UltraScale+ device that captures, infers, displays and reports over MQTT. The speckle decorrelates within tens of seconds at constant temperature, and a press can change it as much as a 1 degree Celsius rise. The node averages each 20 s window and feeds two planes, the mean pattern and a 19-dimensional temporal-feature map, to a 61.6k-parameter int8 convolutional neural network (CNN) that treats presses as hard negatives and runs in the programmable logic at 565 microseconds per frame. On a 59-session, 70,148-window dataset, session-held-out validation gives a pooled AUC of 0.961 against 0.876 for decorrelation, no alarm during the hold or the 45 s rebound in 23 press trials against 6 and 16, and a mean per-fold step detection of 83.8% at 0.4 false alarms per hour.
item.dc:creator: Xuezhi Lou, Weipeng Zhang, Zhibai Zhang, Liyuan Ren

item.title: From Surface Lakes to Subsurface Signatures in Antarctica with BIOMASS P-Band TomoSAR
item.description: arXiv:2611.28189v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spaceborne remote sensing of the cryosphere is fundamental to map ice structure and dynamics. Accurate mass balance estimation requires a better understanding of melt/refreeze processes and firn hydrology, whereas spaceborne optical and Radar sensors are mostly limited to near-surface observations. The BIOMASS P-band Synthetic Aperture Radar, launched by European Space Agency in 2025, provides an unprecedented opportunity to gain a more direct access to englacial processes, thanks to the 70 cm wavelength paired with polarimetry, interferometry and tomography. This paper investigates subsurface beneath a region of historical supraglacial lake activity with BIOMASS tomography, at the Riiser-Larsen Ice Shelf in East Antarctica. The main result is that subsurface scattering appears to be related to historical supraglacial lake recurrence, with structural and depth variations over time. This suggests that recurrent supraglacial lake activity may leave persistent hydrological signatures within the firn. Overall, this study highlights the potential of gaining valuable insights into ice sheet hydrology with P-band.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Banda

item.title: CHARMS250V1: A Cryogenic Front-End ASIC for Low-Noise Readout of Charge or Light Signals in Noble Liquid Detectors
item.description: arXiv:2611.28269v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This work presents the design and measurement results of CHARMS250V1, a next-generation cryogenic front-end application specific integrated circuit (ASIC) developed using a 65 nm CMOS process. It is designed for low-noise readout of charge or light signals generated in noble liquid detectors. CHARMS250V1 is a single channel prototype whose design in the future will be integrated within a 16-channel ASIC. It comprises pre-amplification and pulse shaping stages that provide programmable charge gain between 4.3 mV/fC and 25 mV/fC, peaking time programmable between 250 ns and 2 us, and programmable baseline of either 200 mV or 900 mV for processing of unipolar and bipolar signals, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Prashansa Mukim, Shanshan Gao, Hucheng Chen, Grzegorz W. Deptuch, Jack Fried, Niccolo' Gallice, Dominik Gorni, Lingyun Ke, Giovanni Pinaroli, Sergio Rescia, Chao Zhang

item.title: Benchmarking EEG feature families for ADHD research in children and adolescents: performance and explainability across attention tasks
item.description: arXiv:2611.28299v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder varies in presentation. Diagnosis requires clinical and developmental assessment. Reproducible electroencephalography measures may complement clinical and behavioural characterisation, but differing feature definitions and evaluation methods hinder comparison. We compared seven feature families and four combinations across attention tasks and assessed the stability of held-out explanations. Two serious games yielded four overlapping attention-task cohorts of 123-140 participants each. Repeated nested participant-held-out evaluation assessed recruitment-group discrimination. Exploratory paired participant-cluster bootstrap tests corrected for multiplicity in two separate families: 72 individual-task contrasts and 18 fusion contrasts. For eight configurations selected after inspecting predictive results, we explained held-out native probabilities before calibration. In the strongest task context, the highest configuration mean AUROC over three repetitions was 0.773, with a fixed-prediction 95% interval of 0.692-0.854 unadjusted for selecting the maximum. Precision, sensitivity and specificity were 0.740, 0.556 and 0.861. In that task, the paired AUROC difference for connectivity minus spectral features averaged +0.2083 across six classifiers and the common 8 s and 16 s durations, with pointwise 95% CI 0.1076-0.3072 and adjusted p = 0.0036. F4-AF4 beta-band coherence led repetition-level attribution summaries in five selected procedures and was selected in every fit. Other contexts showed weaker discrimination and less consistent retention of leading scientific inputs. No general classifier winner emerged. Connectivity and its recurring coherence input warrant independent replication, but do not justify a universal feature recommendation. These exploratory findings do not establish causal task effects, disease mechanisms or diagnostic validity.
